To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the in-gap Andeev conductance of a quantum dot embedded between a superconductor and metallic reservoirs is enhanced by emission/abosorption of bosonic excitations; (2) the interference effects between the in-gap Andrev states are manifested in the differential conductace; and (3) the interference effects are enhanced for the non-linear regime of the bias voltage.
the subgap Andreev states can be substantially enhanced and manipulated by the emission/absorption processes of bosonic quasiparticles.

the Andreev states of a quantum dot embedded between two superconductors can be strongly enhanced by coupling to external bosons and that the interference effects of the in-gap states are measurable in transport properties of the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between quantum interference and bosonic excitations in the subgap spectrum of a quantum dot.
the study of Andreev transport through a quantum dot embedded between two superconductors.
the study of Andreev states and transport in hybrid structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantum dot embedded in the superconducting circuit can be used as a sensitive probe to detect external bosonic quasiparticles, which are otherwise difficult to measure.
the quantum dot coupled to superconductors is a promising platform for the realization of the quantum interference of Andreev states and the emission/absorption processes of bosonic quasiparticles.
the subgap Andreev spectrum of the dot can be substantially modified by emission/absorbtion of bosonic quata.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Andreev transport properties of a single-level quantum dot embedded between normal and superconducting reservoirs can be significantly modified by the emission and absorption of bosonic quasiparticles.
the Andreev states can be manipulated by external bosonic quants, such as photons, phonons, and magnons.
the subgap conductance can be enhanced by a factor of 2 to 3 in comparison with the conductance in the absence of the boson emission/absorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Andreev states can be controlled by external bosonic quasiparticles, such as photons or phonons, thus providing a new way of manipulating the transport in hybrid superconducting devices.
the Andreev states in the quantum dot can be manipulated by coupling it to external bosonic reservoirs.
the interference of Andreev states in a quantum dot can be controlled by external bosonic fields.
